brief.title: Mint combinatorial search cells and rotating 8-path query plans across domains
brief.plain_summary: Cross domain facets with intents, angles, stacks, industry verticals, platforms, cross-domain hybrids and injected phrases, attaching negative false-positive guards and page-1 cursors.
brief.outcome: SHA-256-pinned combinatorial cell catalog and rotating path set.

domain_seed_spec.description: Pin of selected domain seeds and optional custom injected phrases.

output_store.description: Store for the produced nouns. The default is a placeholder; use the store your owner assigned.

output_contract.delivery: Write produced nouns surface_only under your own authenticated surface, which is the requester's assigned surface, so the requester and that surface's reviewers can read them. Never use public_commons or allowlist other surfaces. Return every produced noun's pin in output.artifacts; add its value when the requester asks for inline delivery.

outcome_meanings.niche_cells_minted: The declared nouns were produced and every deterministic acceptance check passed.
outcome_meanings.no_change: The evidence does not justify producing or changing anything. Say why.

acceptance_checks.check: mint_combinatorial_niche_catalog reproduces catalog_sha256 and cell_count with zero duplicate cell IDs.

creates.nouns: The worker writes the nouns listed in output_contract.produces and returns their pins.
creates.verbs: The worker proposes follow-up verbs in output.proposed_verbs, such as a breakdown into smaller verbs or a research follow-up, with the pins they need. Proposals are never enqueued by the worker; an authorized requester enqueues the ones worth doing.

required: Cross each domain's facets against intents, angles, technology stacks, industry verticals and cross-domain hybrids.
Attach negative guard terms (-interview -leetcode -homework) and initialize page_cursor=1..5.
Return follow-up work the results justify as proposed_verbs and nouns worth creating later as proposed_nouns. Never enqueue them yourself; an authorized requester decides which to run.

brief.title: Score candidates on 8 axes, benchmark query-family yield and independently review admissions
brief.plain_summary: Score candidates separately on relevance, popularity, commonality, usefulness, value, freeness, activity and rarity, retire query families below 5 percent on-topic yield, and require a distinct reviewer before admitting open-licensed tools.
brief.outcome: Conforming 8-axis evaluation, query-family benchmark and distinct-reviewer admission receipt.
